biggest_gap.title: The screen permission gate does not check keyboard actions: Ctrl+S on a read-only record can send a save and every gate passes
biggest_gap.detail: The product is keyboard-first, so its shortcuts are its main controls. The form kernel (web/src/kernel/forms) decides who may save twice: the `forms.save`/`forms.saveEnter` shortcuts are enabled only when the form is editable, and useRecordForm.save() returns early without canEdit. If both checks are lost, a read-only user's Ctrl+S sends PUT. All 268 web unit tests still pass, as do the 22 screen plant self-tests and the e2e suite. The existing test 'shows a record read-only … no save' presses Ctrl+S but asserts nothing afterwards. The gate should press every registered form and list chord (save, save-enter, discard, new, delete and so on) on a screen whose user lacks the permission, assert that no request other than GET leaves, and be plant-tested against this fault. Every server-side plant this round was caught, including round 1's L2/P1/P2 misses. Separately, and most visible to users, CSV/XLSX exports stop silently at 20,000 rows (see other findings).
biggest_gap.evidence: plants/web-plants.sh, block W2: in RecordForm.tsx `enabled: editable` becomes `enabled: true` on forms.save, and in useRecordForm.ts `if (!current.canEdit || busy)` becomes `if (busy)`. Result: vitest 268/268, tenancy-plant-self-test 17/17 caught, identity 5/5 caught (plants/web-plants.log). plants/web-w2-probe.sh adds `expect(calls.filter(c => c.method !== 'GET')).toEqual([])` after the Ctrl+S in forms.test.tsx:170. It passes unplanted, and with W2 it fails with 'expected [ PUT /api/things/t1 ] to deeply equal []' (plants/web-w2-probe.log).

other_findings: CSV and XLSX exports stop silently at 20,000 rows. GET /api/reports/lists/identity.users?format=csv&language=ar on the demo (100,004 users) gives exactly 20,000 data rows (users-ar.csv, 20,001 lines). There is no note in the file and no response header, and the XLSX autofilter ends at row 20,001. The JSON says matchCount 100004 and truncated true, but the downloads say nothing. Meanwhile the reports screen tells the user 'the whole list is printed from here' (06). An accountant exporting the main 100,000-row list gets 20% of it without knowing. PDFs cap at 2,000 rows and do say so.
